text: An ElastiCache service update for a node-based cluster: a patch AWS makes available under a name. Its type is `security-update`, `engine-update` (patches or minor engine updates for the current engine version) or `engine-major-version-update`. Service updates are cumulative: the latest one includes any not yet applied.

This cannot be expressed in code. A service update is applied with `batch-apply-update-action` or by ElastiCache in the maintenance window; Terraform and CloudFormation have no argument for it. From Valkey 7.2 and Redis OSS 6.0 ElastiCache manages the patch version itself, so the code's engine version (major.minor) does not change and nothing drifts.
A CVE is named here only when an AWS security bulletin names this service update. Otherwise the update's own severity (critical, important, medium, low) is what AWS gives.

Nodes are updated in turn. With replicas the cluster stays available for reads, and writes pause for the few seconds of each failover; existing client connections are terminated, so clients must reconnect with retries and exponential backoff. A single node, or a group without Multi-AZ, is unavailable while its primary is updated. On Memcached, engine version upgrades clear all cache data; AWS does not say on the pages read whether a service update on Memcached nodes does.

Each update has a Recommended Apply By Date (critical: within 14 days, important: 30, medium: 60, low: 90). When its "Auto-update after due date" is Yes, ElastiCache schedules it in the cluster's maintenance window after that date; when it is No it is never applied automatically. ElastiCache reserves the right to patch on your behalf for a critical security vulnerability.

The person running this needs `elasticache:DescribeServiceUpdates`, `elasticache:DescribeUpdateActions`, `elasticache:BatchApplyUpdateAction`, `elasticache:DescribeReplicationGroups` and `elasticache:CreateSnapshot` on this replication group.
Only an update with status available or scheduled can be applied. Read its severity, type and whether it auto-applies after the due date.
The replication group must be `available`. Read whether Multi-AZ and automatic failover are on, how many replicas each shard has, and the maintenance window. Apply in a period of low write traffic.
Automatic backups are off unless the snapshot retention limit is above zero. Take a manual backup first (Valkey and Redis OSS; Memcached has no persistence).
ElastiCache console, Region {region} > Service updates > select `{update}` > select the cluster `{id}` > Apply now.
Apply the service update to the replication group.
The update action's status goes from in-progress to complete (shown for 7 days). Check the replication group is `available` and clients reconnected.
A running update can be stopped: nodes already in progress finish, the others are left on the old version and the update can be resumed later. Nodes that were updated can't be reverted.

An engine version upgrade of the cache (a new major or minor version, or the move from Redis OSS to Valkey). ElastiCache never starts one by itself while a version is supported: it is started by changing the engine version.
This has a code equivalent: the engine version of the replication group (and the engine, for Redis OSS to Valkey).

Change `engine_version` on the `aws_elasticache_replication_group`. For version 7 and higher write major.minor (`7.2`), never a patch version; for 6 write `6.2` or `6.x`. A major version jump also needs a compatible `parameter_group_name`. Moving to Valkey sets `engine = "valkey"` together with an explicit `engine_version`. `aws_elasticache_cluster` accepts only `memcached` and `redis`.

`apply_immediately` defaults to `false`: the upgrade waits for the next maintenance window and the plan keeps showing a difference until it runs. Any attribute change that re-creates the resource is applied immediately whatever `apply_immediately` says.

An `engine_version` increase is in place. A decrease is not: the provider re-creates the replication group when the version is lowered, which destroys the data. Never lower the version to roll back. CoderHelm also refuses a change to `replication_group_id`, `subnet_group_name`, `at_rest_encryption_enabled`, `kms_key_id` or `port` in an upgrade change.

Change `EngineVersion` on the `AWS::ElastiCache::ReplicationGroup` (Update requires: No interruption, meaning no replacement; the service still fails over). Moving to Valkey sets `Engine: valkey` and needs a parameter group. `AWS::ElastiCache::CacheCluster` accepts only `memcached` and `redis`, and changing its `Engine` is a replacement.

These resources have no `ApplyImmediately` property. AWS does not say on the pages read whether a version change from CloudFormation applies at once or in the maintenance window: plan for it to start when the stack update runs.

Replacement properties include `AtRestEncryptionEnabled`, `KmsKeyId`, `CacheSubnetGroupName`, `Port`, `ReplicationGroupId`, `SnapshotName`, `NetworkType` and `DataTieringEnabled`. Changing `NumNodeGroups` or `NodeGroupConfiguration` without `UpdatePolicy: UseOnlineResharding: true` replaces the whole replication group.

From Redis OSS 5.0.6 the cluster stays available for reads during the upgrade and for writes except during each failover, which lasts a few seconds; existing client connections are terminated. A single node, or a group without Multi-AZ, has its primary unavailable during the upgrade. A Memcached version upgrade always clears all cache data.

A pending scale-up blocks an engine upgrade. A single node or non-Multi-AZ group needs enough free memory for a snapshot. A major version jump needs a parameter group compatible with the new version. An encrypted group can't move to a version without encryption support.
The upgrade makes a best effort to keep the data. Automatic backups are off unless the snapshot retention limit is above zero: take a manual backup first.
Upgrade the replication group in its next maintenance window (use `--apply-immediately` to upgrade now).

You can't downgrade to an earlier engine version: the only way is to delete the group and create it again on the earlier version, restoring a backup. The one exception AWS documents is rolling Valkey 7.2 back to Redis OSS 7.1.
